title: Protocol for Studying Microplastic Intake in Stranded Cetaceans
author: Tania Montoto-Martinez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcfxitpn

steps.title: Seal thoracic oesophagus
steps.instruction: Locate the final part of the oesophagus between the lungs, tie a tight knot with string around it, repeat the ligature about 5 cm cranially, and cut between the two knotted areas.

steps.title: Extract and seal proximal oesophagus
steps.instruction: After block extraction of thoracic organs, locate the proximal oesophagus (post‑laryngeal appendix), seal it with the same ligature method, cut the sealed area, dissect the first digestive segment, remove the oesophagus, rinse it externally and set aside.

steps.title: Seal distal intestine
steps.instruction: Open the abdominal cavity and place two ligatures of string around the final intestinal portion, as done for the oesophagus.

steps.title: Prepare necropsy table drainage
steps.instruction: Connect the necropsy table drainage to a stack of three metal sieves (1000 µm, 500 µm and 200 µm) to retain washed gastrointestinal contents.

steps.title: Extract gastrointestinal package
steps.instruction: Remove the gastrointestinal block, separate it from pancreas, spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes, then separate stomach together with the duodenal ampulla from the rest of the intestine.

steps.title: Seal duodenum and dissect intestine
steps.instruction: Tie two ligatures around the proximal duodenum leaving ~5 cm between them, cut the central area of this space, carefully separate the intestine from the mesentery, and rinse the stomach/duodenal ampulla externally on one side and the intestinal package on the other.

steps.title: Implement contamination controls
steps.instruction: Follow the protocol’s Guidelines & Warnings, keep the work area clean, use a new air‑control filter beside the operation area between each compartment, and minimise exposure time of digestive contents.

steps.title: Empty digestive contents
steps.instruction: One by one, empty the oesophagus, stomach, duodenal ampulla and intestine into separate trays, cleaning the table thoroughly and placing a fresh air‑control filter before proceeding to the next compartment.

steps.title: Rinse lumens with filtered water
steps.instruction: Rinse the interior of each gastrointestinal section with filtered water, allowing all digestive traces to remain on the trays.

steps.title: Macroscopic examination and sampling
steps.instruction: Examine each GIT section macroscopically and collect samples for histopathology and, if needed, microbiology.

steps.title: Retain material on sieves
steps.instruction: Allow the emptied digestive material to remain on the stacked sieves (1000 µm, 500 µm, 200 µm) for subsequent processing.

steps.title: Extract organic remains
steps.instruction: Manually extract organic remains, place them in airtight containers and store at –20 °C for later laboratory study.

steps.title: Extract and preserve parasites
steps.instruction: Manually collect all parasites, place them in organ‑specific containers, label each with the organ name, preserve in 70 % alcohol, and assign a parasite‑load index (Mild 1‑10, Moderate 20‑50, Intermediate 50‑100, High 100‑500, Massive >500).

steps.title: Extract macro‑waste
steps.instruction: Manually extract non‑organic waste retained on the 5 mm sieve, place it in organ‑specific containers and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Check sieve for diet indicators
steps.instruction: Inspect the sieve to ensure no diet indicators (e.g., otoliths, crystals) remain.

steps.title: Digest organic material with KOH
steps.instruction: Pour the stomach content of each GIT compartment into a glass beaker and add 10 % KOH solution at three times the sample volume; allow degradation to occur.

steps.title: Filter digested sample
steps.instruction: Using a vacuum pump, filter the degraded material onto Whatman® glass microfiber filters (Grade GF/F, 47 mm).

steps.title: Microscopic analysis of filters
steps.instruction: Observe each filter under a microscope with airborne‑contamination controls, photograph and measure identified particles following Lusher et al. (2014) guidelines.
